recommended_fix.guidance: Ship every consent control unselected, and record consent only after the Data Principal takes a clear affirmative action, such as ticking the box themselves. Do not default a consent value to true in the model, the form or the API, because §6(1) requires that clear affirmative action. Apply the same rule to any consent set during sign-up, import or migration.

value.fix: Remove the `checked` attribute from the consent checkbox so it starts unticked. Consent is only valid when the user ticks the box themselves (DPDP §6(1)). Keep `required` if this consent is truly needed for the service, or remove it if the user may refuse. The template should be: `<input class="form-check-input" type="checkbox" name="consent_transactions" id="id_consent_transactions" required style="width: 2.5em; height: 1.25em;">`. In the backend, make sure nothing else defaults this consent to true: the model field should use `default=False`, the Django form field should not set `initial=True`, and the API should not fill in a missing value as true. On submit, set consent to true only if `consent_transactions` is actually in the POST data (`'consent_transactions' in request.POST`, or `form.cleaned_data` with a `BooleanField` that has no initial value). Store when consent was given (timestamp) alongside it. Check sign-up, import and migration code for any consent set to true without the user's action, and reset those records to false until users confirm.

recommended_fix.guidance: List nomination alongside the other Data Principal rights in every in-repo notice or rights page, and provide a route for a Data Principal to nominate another individual who can exercise those rights on their behalf. §14 provides for nomination, and Rule 14(4) sets how it is made.

value.fix: The template claims "DPDP Act-aligned data handling", but no in-repo notice or rights page mentions the right to nominate under DPDP Act §14. Add a nomination entry to every privacy notice and Data Principal rights page, next to the rights to access, correct, erase and seek grievance redressal. For example: {% trans "Right to nominate: you may nominate another individual to exercise your rights under the DPDP Act if you die or become incapacitated (Section 14)." %}. Then build a working way to nominate, following the manner set by Rule 14(4): (1) a nominee form or view, reachable from the account or privacy settings and linked from the rights page, that records the nominee's name, contact details and relationship; (2) a Nominee model linked to the user, with created and updated timestamps, plus the ability to change or withdraw the nomination at any time; (3) a process for a nominee to submit a rights request with proof of death or incapacity, sent to the grievance or DPO contact for checking. Until nomination is listed and the form works, change the badge text to something that doesn't claim alignment, such as "Privacy-focused data handling".

value.reason: The flagged line, templates/landing.html:1431, is only a marketing tagline: "DPDP Act-aligned data handling". It is not a notice telling Data Principals what their rights are. It lists no rights at all, so it can't be said to leave out the right to nominate under Section 14(1) or Rule 14(4). The positive example is different: it lists rights (access, correction, erasure) and omits nomination. The evidence contains no list of rights, so the RIG-04-rights-notice pattern doesn't apply to this line. Whether a real rights notice elsewhere on the site omits nomination can't be judged from this evidence and would need its own finding.

    ip_address = models.GenericIPAddressField(null=True, blank=True)
    user_agent = models.TextField(null=True, blank=True)

    def __str__(self):

value.assessment: The Evidence shows a DPDP consent design that is partly in place but has clear gaps. Server-side enforcement is established. A redirect middleware is registered in settings and sends users without consent_granted to the dpdp_consent page. Every PostHog client.capture and client.identify call is checked with analytics_consent_given() before it runs. Specific consent is not met on either grant path (signup.html and dpdp_consent.html). The transactions and device toggles are pre-checked and required, and email consent is a hidden input fixed to "on". The signup notice also says toggling each item is required to register. So the user cannot choose per Purpose, and the only real actions are the age checkbox and the submit button. Each grant writes a ConsentEvent with user, action, a single generic purpose label, version, timestamp, IP and user agent. However, the record is flagged incomplete and is not linked to the itemised Purposes, so it is not determinable whether it is adequate proof. An itemised notice comes before the signup grant (before_grant true), but no notice resolved for the dpdp_consent path comes before its grant. For either path, the Evidence does not show that the notice covers how to withdraw consent, how to complain to the Board, or language options. Withdrawal is only possible by deleting the whole account. Neither the grant nor the withdrawal path has a resolved step count, so comparable ease cannot be judged. PostHog calls are gated against future processing, but erasing data already sent to the Data Processor is unresolved. The privacy policy itself says analytics data already collected is not deleted when the user changes their choice. Verifiable parental consent was not resolved, and only an age self-declaration was found.

criteria.reason: ConsentEvent records are created on both grant paths (expenses/forms.py:911 'Signup Data Collection' and expenses/views/misc.py:448 'Terms and Data Collection'). They store user, action, consent_version, timestamp, ip_address and user_agent. Every record is flagged complete=false and has no linked purpose_ids. Each one uses a single generic purpose label rather than the three itemised Purposes, and does not capture choices per control. The account-deletion withdrawal path does not show a WITHDRAWN record; such records appear only for family household flows. So the Evidence does not establish whether these records are enough to prove notice and consent.

On both signup.html and dpdp_consent.html, consent_transactions and consent_device are pre-checked and required (default_selected true), and consent_email is a hidden input with value="on" that the user never sees or controls. The signup notice says 'Toggling each is required to complete your registration.' The user therefore cannot give or refuse consent for each Purpose separately. The only affirmative actions are confirm_age and submit, which does not meet the standard of specific, unconditional consent given by a clear affirmative action for each specified Purpose.

DPDPAConsentMiddleware is registered in finance_tracker/settings.py:146. It redirects to dpdp_consent when profile.consent_granted is false (expenses/middleware.py:147-148). PostHog capture and identify are each preceded by a server-side analytics_consent_given() check (expenses/posthog_utils.py:108 and 125). All of these enforcement points are flagged server_side=true.

Withdrawal happens through WithdrawConsentView (settings/consent/withdraw/), a single form submit that deletes the account. Withdrawing per Purpose is not possible. Both the grant and withdrawal paths have start_template and step_count set to null, and step counts cannot be compared without a common, statically resolved starting point. Comparable ease therefore cannot be established.

Future calls to the PostHog Data Processor (client.capture and client.identify) are gated server-side by a consent check. The processor_propagation state, however, records that earlier transfers and deletion are unresolved. Calling dispatch_account_deletion does not prove that any processor erasure happened. The privacy policy notice (templates/privacy_policy.html:154) states that 'Analytics data already collected is not deleted when you change your choice.' That points to a possible gap in causing the Data Processor to stop processing or erase, but the Evidence does not show what happens when the account is deleted.

On signup, an itemised notice (templates/account/signup.html:105, before_grant true) with linked Purposes appears before the submit button. On the dpdp_consent path, the general notice (line 12) has before_grant null, and the version notice (line 88) has before_grant false. Neither linked notice is shown to state how to withdraw consent, how to exercise rights, or how to complain to the Board. That information appears only in the privacy policy (notice 333), whose before_grant is null and which is not linked to the grant. No option to read the notice in English or an Eighth Schedule language is established (language null).

Both the child gate and the parental verification are in state 'not determinable'. The only related evidence is a required confirm_age self-declaration checkbox (age 18 or older, not stored) on both grant paths. No mechanism for verifiable parental consent was found, and whether the audience includes children, or whether age or date of birth is collected, was not established.
